title: Elicitation-Gap Uncertainty x Conditional Safety Triggers: Error-Propagation Through Policy Logic

original_idea.body:
# Elicitation-Gap Uncertainty x Conditional Safety Triggers: Error-Propagation Through Policy Logic

**Problem:** Failure mode A: capability elicitation is noisy. Failure mode B: responsible-scaling policies treat a single eval number as a crisp trigger. Measurement uncertainty propagates into binary policy decisions.

**Direction:** On one open model and one safety-relevant task, run several elicitation strategies and record the spread, propagate through a stylized threshold-trigger rule to compute the probability of a wrong governance decision. Output an error-budget recommendation.

**Why it matters:** Bridges measurement noise and policy logic, giving a principled elicitation budget. Statistics-forward, beginner-appropriate.

**Relevant context:** Open Problems in Technical AI Governance (arXiv:2407.14981); sandbagging/elicitation literature (arXiv:2406.07358).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: noisy triggers can misfire on scaling decisions, a recognized critical pathway, with a concrete error-budget deliverable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Few elicitation strategies + simple error propagation on one model; guided and tractable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment (one model, one task) with clear success criterion (probability of wrong decision).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open model, statistics-forward, weak lab incentive to publish elicitation-noise critiques.

low_compute.reasoning: A few elicitation runs on one open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Elicitation noise is studied; propagating it through trigger logic as an error budget may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Elicitation-gap work exists but the error-budget-through-trigger framing may be open.
